title: Museo del Prado: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty paintings of rulers, workers, witnesses and people under threat.
introduction:
In *Las Meninas*, the painter looks out of the room toward a position that may also belong to the royal sitters. In Goya's execution scene, the victims expose their faces while the soldiers turn their backs. These are very different paintings, but both make the viewer's position part of the problem.

The selection follows such distributions of visibility and power. A key passes between commanders; a cardinal needs almost no setting to establish rank; workers occupy the foreground of a myth. Religious images and scenes of violence ask who supports a body, who watches it, and who remains unseen. This is a set of comparisons within the collection, not a room-by-room itinerary.
visitNote: Check the Prado's current collection pages for room locations and temporary changes. The museum also offers its own tours and learning resources. Use those to plan your route through the building.

books.title: Velazquez
books.author: S. L. Bensusan
books.note: A short illustrated study of Velázquez, published in English in 1907. It records an earlier view of the painter's work; the Prado's current entries should take precedence for dates and attributions.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: Leonardo's notes on observation, proportion and painting, in an older English translation. They offer background on a painter's practical problems; this book does not discuss the Prado's collection.

selectionNote: Artline selected these works from documented museum holdings. The selection is independent of the museum, and individual works may be on loan or off display. Dates and attributions retain the qualifications in the linked records.

works.title: Las Meninas
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: The large canvas withholds what Velázquez is painting. Instead, his outward gaze, the royal figures in the rear mirror and the open doorway establish competing positions around the visible group. The room is convincing enough to enter imaginatively, but the viewer's place within it remains unsettled. That uncertainty belongs to the portrait's construction, not to a missing piece of scenery.

works.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
works.catalogueTitle: The Garden of Earthly Delights Triptych
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: Before pursuing an individual fruit or hybrid creature, follow the changing conditions across the panels. Open landscape gives way to crowded pleasure, then to darkness and punishment. Bodies recur, but what surrounds and happens to them alters drastically. The hinges separate stages of the argument even when the abundance of small incidents makes the eye reluctant to move on.

works.title: The Descent from the Cross
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: The Virgin's collapsing body repeats the inclination of Christ's. Around this correspondence, other mourners perform distinct actions: supporting, bending, wiping tears. Grief is shared without being made uniform. The shallow golden enclosure gives the figures little room to withdraw, bringing their gestures together almost as a relief while preserving the particular pressure of each pair of hands.

works.title: The Third of May 1808
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: The lantern exposes the prisoners and leaves the firing squad largely without faces. White shirt and raised arms isolate one man between the dead before him and those still waiting. Goya gives the sequence of execution a spatial form. The soldiers' repeated backs and weapons confront people whose individual reactions remain visible, making the exchange deliberately unequal.

works.title: The Surrender of Breda
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: An army's victory is concentrated into the transfer of a small key. Spears, soldiers and the scarred landscape establish the event's scale, but the commanders' encounter determines how victory is presented. The victor's conduct toward the defeated man matters as much as possession of the town. A restrained gesture carries an otherwise expansive public account of power.

works.title: The Spinners, or the Fable of Arachne
works.catalogueTitle: The Spinners, or the Fable of Arachne
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: The finished tapestry is farther away than the labour of making thread. Workers and a spinning wheel occupy the dim foreground; a brighter raised space opens behind them onto the mythic subject. The division makes production difficult to overlook. Cloth appears both as something handled through practical skill and as a surface capable of carrying an elaborate story.

works.title: Emperor Charles V at Mühlberg
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: The battle is represented through a mounted ruler rather than through fighting troops. Armour, lance and command of the horse make military success part of Charles's bearing. Red cloth connects rider and mount against the glowing sky. With so few competing actors, the portrait can present an entire victory as something concentrated in the emperor's person.

works.title: The Cardinal
works.credit: Rafael Sanzio. The Cardinal. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Red identifies the sitter's office before a setting can explain it. The pale face and white sleeve interrupt that broad colour, giving small changes of position considerable force. Raphael establishes authority through a direct gaze and controlled turn of the body. Compare the economy of this arrangement with the many costumes and faces in Goya's royal family.

works.title: Self-Portrait, 1498
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: Dürer's carefully dressed figure occupies the role of a distinguished sitter. The gloved hands remain composed, while curls and fabric receive close attention. A window gives the portrait a distance beyond the body. This turned, socially presented figure differs from the later frontal self-portrait in Munich; the two pictures make separate claims through posture and setting.

works.title: The Adoration of the Shepherds
works.credit: Adoración de los pastores. El Greco; El Greco; [1]; © Madrid, Museo Nacional del Prado. Source terms: https://www.museodelprado.es/en/legal-information. Commons asserts: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full supplied composition.
works.license: Prado reproduction terms; Commons label: Public domain
works.description: The tall format puts the gathering under upward pressure. Elongated bodies bend toward the child and extend into the space above, with light linking faces and robes through the crowded scene. Exact physical positions can be difficult to untangle. Colour and illumination supply another route through the group, keeping the devotional centre legible within the movement.

works.title: Saturn
works.medium: Mixed technique on a wall, transferred to canvas
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: There is almost nowhere else to look. Darkness removes the setting, leaving grasping hands, a wide-eyed face and the mutilated body pressed to the mouth. The myth has been stripped of a surrounding assembly of gods or witnesses. Violence fills the available encounter with the image, without an explanatory spectator to stand between the act and its viewer.

works.title: The Naked Maja
works.credit: Francisco de Goya. The Naked Maja. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The reclining figure meets the viewer's gaze with her hands placed behind her head. White pillows extend the body's horizontal position against the darkness. Comparison with *The Clothed Maja* can begin with what remains stable: posture, setting and the outward look. Clothing changes the painted surface considerably without providing a simple explanation of the sitter's expression.

works.title: The Clothed Maja
works.credit: Francisco Goya. The Clothed Maja. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The white costume introduces folds and seams along the reclining body, while the darker jacket interrupts its length. These are compositional changes as well as a difference in coverage. Keeping the related nude nearby in mind helps separate the work performed by clothing from that performed by pose. The direct gaze does not disappear beneath the added ornament.

works.title: Apollo in the Forge of Vulcan
works.catalogueTitle: Apollo in the Forge of Vulcan
works.credit: Diego Velázquez. Apollo in the Forge of Vulcan. Image credit: Diego Velázquez; Own work , user:Luestling. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: The news arrives before the workers can put their tools away. Apollo's entrance interrupts a sequence of bodily tasks, leaving each man caught in a different position. Myth becomes intelligible through that broken routine. Surprise does not require a repeated theatrical gesture when a turning head or a suddenly arrested hand can show work being stopped.

works.title: David and Goliath
works.credit: Caravaggio. David and Goliath. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: David bends over the severed head rather than standing clear of it in triumph. His face turns down, and the illuminated arms emphasise what he must still handle after the battle. The dark setting leaves little space for spectators or public celebration. Victory has an awkward physical aftermath, which Caravaggio keeps close to the front of the picture.

works.title: The Triumph of Death
works.credit: El triunfo de la Muerte. Pieter Bruegel el Viejo; Pieter Brueghel the Elder; Museo del Prado; © Madrid, Museo Nacional del Prado. Source terms: https://www.museodelprado.es/en/legal-information. Commons asserts: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full supplied composition.
works.license: Prado reproduction terms; Commons label: Public domain
works.description: Following one attempted escape leads into another catastrophe. Bruegel disperses the action across ranks and settings, making accumulation more important than a single protagonist. Fires and ruined buildings continue the threat into the distance. The many small episodes offer ample detail but little relief: the eye can travel widely without finding a part of society outside death's reach.

works.title: The Family of Charles IV
works.credit: Francisco Goya. The Family of Carlos IV. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Ceremonial clothes display a dynasty, while separate faces resist becoming a uniform emblem. Goya places himself in shadow at the side, allowing the royal group to occupy the breadth of the canvas. Unlike the uncertain exchanges in *Las Meninas*, this arrangement holds its sitters before sustained inspection. Individuality need not be mistaken for evidence of a hidden caricature.

works.title: The Feast of Bacchus
works.credit: Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; file-specific public-domain notice (PD-Art). Original held at Museo Nacional del Prado. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: Bacchus's pale, partly undressed body remains distinct from his clothed companions, but everyone occupies the same gathering. A wreath supplies ceremony while nearby faces and everyday dress pull the event toward an ordinary drinking party. The god does not require a separate heavenly zone. The painting's difference of register happens among bodies sitting close together.

works.title: Christ Crucified
works.credit: Diego Velazquez. Cristo crucificado. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The dark ground removes almost all narrative surroundings. Christ's lowered head and balanced limbs are left to establish weight against the cross. This concentration gives the image a different pace from El Greco's crowded devotional gatherings. Light does not lead through a succession of figures; it holds attention on one body and the fact of its suspension.

works.title: The Trinity
works.credit: La Trinidad. El Greco; El Greco; [2]; © Madrid, Museo Nacional del Prado. Source terms: https://www.museodelprado.es/en/legal-information. Commons asserts: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full supplied composition.
works.license: Prado reproduction terms; Commons label: Public domain
works.description: The Father's support makes Christ's dead weight visible even within the heavenly gathering. The body pulls diagonally across the composition while angels and robes draw attention upward toward the dove. Those directions do not fully cancel each other. El Greco allows the material difficulty of holding a body to remain inside the theological image.

closingSections.title: Choose a comparison before a route
paragraphs: Two paintings can sustain a visit: the royal groups, the Majas, or the different treatments of Christ's body. Their differences become clearer with time than with a longer checklist. Confirm current display and access through the Prado before planning around a particular work; collection membership alone does not establish availability.
